newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bryant pleads guilty to Port Arthur massacre.
newsitem.headline: Bryant pleads guilty to Port Arthur massacre.

text.p: Martin Bryant, the man accused of the worst mass killing in modern Australian history, pleaded guilty on Thursday to all 35 murders at the Port Arthur historic site in April, reversing an earlier plea of not guilty.
Bryant, 29, laughed and smirked as he pleaded guilty to a total of 72 charges, including the 35 murders in an appearance in the Supreme Court of Tasmania to discuss his trial.

As each charge was read out, Bryant either leaned forward towards a microphone and mumbled "guilty" or he looked around the room, eyeballing survivors of the massacre and relatives of the victims and loudly said "guilty".
Judge William Cox adjourned the case until November 19 for a plea of mitigation and sentencing, warning the media against prejudicing Bryant.
Cox said publication of prejudicial material would "commit a grave contempt of this court".
"The accused must be accorded full opportunity to place before me all facts and circumstances relevant to a plea of mitigation," Cox said.
On April 28, Bryant opened fire with a high powered rifle at Port Arthur, a former convict settlement and popular tourist site on Tasmania's southeast coast.
He was arrested the following morning.
On September 30, Bryant pleaded not guilty to a total of 72 charges, including 35 murders, attempted murder, grievous bodily harm, assault and arson.
After the hearing, Bryant's lawyer John Avery declined to say why Bryant had originally pleaded not guilty.
"All I can say is we have been doing a lot of talking over the past few weeks and I am gratified that the right decision has been made," Avery told reporters.
Bryant appeared in court under heavy police protection, with the bomb squad sweeping the court building before his appearance.
